newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, mild growth to continue.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, mild growth to continue.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed in active post-election buying on Tuesday with new gains for blue chips, and market watchers expected a sustained mild rising trend through the week.
"The trading activity is intense and that could last, but I don't expect anything spectacular," said Davor Relja, analyst at Faktor brokerage.
Results of the municipal and regional polls, at which the ruling HDZ won in 18 of 21 counties, came as no big surprise, traders said.
"Stronger buying began five days before, I'm not sure it has anything to do with elections. We expected such results anyway," said Velimir Zelimorski of brokerage FIMA.
Rather than polls, he traced positive events to blue chip Zagrebacka Banka, which released buoyant 1996 results last week and triggered a new wave of investment in Croatia's tiny share market.
Its rise last week in turn boosted hoteliers Istraturist and Jadranturist, in which the bank has majority holdings.
But some other stocks also gained on the back of stronger buying interest.
"Most prices are stabilising now, but some are rising," Zelimorski said.
Six of 19 active issues rose on Tuesday -- first day of trade on the Zagreb Stock Exchange -- seven fell, five were flat and one traded for the first time.
Zagrebacka's ordinary shares added 10 kuna to 2,000 on Tuesday on volume of 2,518.
Another fully-listed issue Pliva firmed five kuna to 475 with 3,272 units changing hands. The company announced a news conference to release its last year's profit on April 18.
"When it does, the market could rise further," said Relja.
Chocolate maker Kras was the day's top gainer, rising 4.77 percent to 461 kuna on volume of 801 shares.
Podravka food concern was the most actively traded issue with 3,310 shares, closing one kuna lower at 308 kuna.
Textile firm Varteks, dipping 10.9 percent with 100 shares sold, led decliners which also included some hotel issues and Zagrebacka's preferred and bearer stocks.

Another loser, the 1-issue of Varazdinska Banka, which last week joined Pliva and Zagrebacka in the Zagreb bourse's first quotation, dropped 2,000 kuna to 49,000, but on a meagre volume of four shares.
Varazdinska's 2-issue, also fully-listed, traded 30 kuna up to 1,450, selling seven shares.
New entry on the parallel bourse list, agricultural firm Mednik, sold 18,833 units in what looked like two pre-arranged deals. It closed at 714.96 kuna.

Volume rose to 30,580 units and turnover to 21 million kuna from last Friday's 17 million. It compares to only a few million kuna a day no earlier than 10 days ago when trade languished ahead of the elections.
